from itertools import permutations

# Categories are determined by adjective meaning. Their relative order is
# inferred only from the supplied examples, not from standard English.
groups = {
    "opinion": "good lovely silly wonderful awful nice ridiculous terrible",
    "purpose": "drinking snorkeling typing exercise eating whittling smoking hiking driving",
    "size": "massive big enormous huge midsize normal-size small large medium-size tiny little",
    "color": "gray yellow maroon violet green indigo black teal cyan crimson blue pink brown aqua",
    "age": "archaic ancient old-fashioned brand-new old new",
    "shape": "spherical square pyramidal circular rectangular prismlike triangular",
    "material": "glass steel iron wool plastic rubber fiberglass wood paper",
    "origin": "vietnamese turkish russian thai bangladeshi iranian ethiopian indian mexican american filipino japanese",
}
category = {
    word: name
    for name, words in groups.items()
    for word in words.split()
}

# Every supplied example containing more than one adjective.
# Nouns are omitted; single-adjective examples impose no ordering constraints.
evidence = [
    "good gray archaic",
    "massive yellow",
    "good drinking",
    "big maroon",
    "enormous violet",
    "glass vietnamese",
    "lovely snorkeling",
    "ancient spherical",
    "old-fashioned spherical",
    "brand-new square",
    "good typing",
    "silly exercise",
    "steel turkish",
    "iron russian",
    "silly snorkeling",
    "huge green",
    "steel thai",
    "brand-new circular",
    "brand-new pyramidal",
    "huge indigo",
    "wonderful whittling",
    "midsize black",
    "steel bangladeshi",
    "wool iranian",
    "ancient rectangular",
    "plastic thai",
    "big black",
    "rubber russian",
    "iron ethiopian",
    "normal-size teal",
    "ridiculous typing",
    "small cyan",
    "huge yellow",
    "awful whittling",
    "old prismlike",
    "silly whittling",
    "terrible smoking",
    "huge crimson",
    "old-fashioned pyramidal",
    "old triangular",
    "ancient spherical",
    "nice snorkeling",
    "big maroon",
    "ancient circular",
    "driving midsize rectangular",
    "steel russian",
    "terrible hiking",
    "large crimson",
    "brand-new spherical",
    "fiberglass indian",
    "normal-size maroon",
]

options = {
    "A": "nice typing big yellow new rectangular wool",
    "B": "silly whittling little gray archaic square vietnamese",
    "C": "mexican medium-size violet ancient spherical typing silly",
    "D": "plastic large blue old-fashioned rectangular whittling good",
    "E": "wood turkish tiny pink archaic prismlike whittling",
    "F": "silly hiking medium-size black old-fashioned spherical mexican steel",
    "G": "terrible eating midsize green brand-new prismlike",
    "H": "filipino paper small violet new spherical snorkeling",
    "I": "snorkeling little brown old circular plastic american",
    "J": "japanese glass midsize aqua brand-new spherical",
}

constraints = set()
for phrase in evidence:
    sequence = [category[word] for word in phrase.split()]
    for i, earlier in enumerate(sequence):
        for later in sequence[i + 1:]:
            constraints.add((earlier, later))

option_sequences = {
    label: [category[word] for word in phrase.split()]
    for label, phrase in options.items()
}

# Exhaustively examine every total category order compatible with all evidence.
models = []
for order in permutations(groups):
    position = {name: i for i, name in enumerate(order)}
    if all(position[a] < position[b] for a, b in constraints):
        correct = "".join(
            label
            for label, sequence in option_sequences.items()
            if all(
                position[a] < position[b]
                for a, b in zip(sequence, sequence[1:])
            )
        )
        models.append(correct or "K")

if not models:
    print("UNSUPPORTED: the inferred category constraints are inconsistent.")
    print("CHECK UNKNOWN")
else:
    print("Compatible category orders:", len(models))
    for label in options:
        count = sum(label in answer for answer in models)
        print(f"{label}: correct in {count}/{len(models)} compatible orders")

    guaranteed = "".join(
        label for label in options
        if all(label in answer for answer in models)
    )
    print("Guaranteed correct choices:", guaranteed or "(none)")
    print("Possible complete answers:", ", ".join(sorted(set(models))))
    print("Submitted answer: K")
    if all(answer != "K" for answer in models):
        print("CHECK FAIL: every compatible order has a correct choice; "
              "in particular, G is guaranteed correct.")
    elif all(answer == "K" for answer in models):
        print("CHECK PASS")
    else:
        print("UNSUPPORTED: the examples do not settle whether K is correct.")
        print("CHECK UNKNOWN")
